items.title: fix: repair release pipelines and add JavaScript-first gates
items.body:
Release-note formatting discarded content after Markdown rules and omitted later PRs, several CI checks hid real failures, and the checked-in dependency locks failed the security workflow. This change repairs those paths and implements every required subissue of #254, including a working opt-in JavaScript-first prerequisite for mixed-language projects.

- Preserve complete release-note Markdown and collect unique PR links across all change entries, while continuing to send release bodies through JSON stdin.
- Queue all main writers without cancellation; update supported action/tool versions; enforce reported lint warnings; detect shell and other code changes; check standalone scripts and hooks with pinned ShellCheck.
- Make preview drift, authentication fallback and summaries reflect actual outcomes. Check Pages/dependency-graph prerequisites with actionable main-branch failures and PR warnings for settings that only a maintainer can change.
- Bound Changesets fixture process trees and cleanup, retain optional timing diagnostics, and avoid early execution-budget termination. Correct status-gate needs parsing and fork-head resolution.
- Refresh npm/Deno locks, remove vulnerable transitive packages, retain an exact reviewed deprecation inventory, and add the patch changeset for the next release.
- Add a callable native JavaScript/parity/regeneration gate with immutable tested-SHA output. The dependency-free mixed-language example supplies real commands and gates all six downstream Rust paths, including native shared-fixture execution. Contributor and agent policy require one coordinator push per validated batch. The example accepts PR checks and trusted main pushes; removing its optional manual trigger fixes all three CodeQL cache-poisoning paths without weakening analysis or the reusable gate's immutable-candidate contract.

The complete requirement-to-implementation/test inventory is in [experiments/issue-254-plan.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-254-a1fc75afdb37/experiments/issue-254-plan.md). The example deliberately translates one complete integer-parity API; its documentation states the supported grammar, refusal behavior and scope.

Reproduction and regression coverage:

- `node --test tests/release-notes-description.test.js tests/release-notes-integration.test.js` exercises multiple changeset entries/sections, nested lists, paragraphs, rules, literal escapes, deduplicated PR links and workflow-commit fallback with the real formatter and offline fixtures.
- `node --test tests/javascript-first-gate.test.js` verifies the safe caller-trigger boundary and runs the actual workflow shell steps in temporary Git repositories. Failed/skipped native checks, missing/partial/carried inventory entries, generated drift, untracked files and moved HEAD block every Rust path; a complete unchanged candidate permits all six at exactly the tested SHA.
- The remaining focused tests execute preview token selection, push/staging outcomes and summaries, Pages/graph API fixtures, OIDC bootstrap diagnostics, process-tree timeouts, the wall-second deadline reproducer and colliding fork/base refs. Workflow assertions preserve job/gate/permissions coverage and the precise actionlint exception.
- On the original PR SHA `5bb14be`, Security run [39917108648](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/39917108648) failed both npm audits. Both updated lockfiles now audit with zero vulnerabilities.

Validation at commit `470e5e451c7c2116fdc89e286fc29bd8118fe5e2` (2026-10-24): all six workflows completed successfully — [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40086413552), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40086413616), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40086413581), [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40086413572), [Example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40086413577), and [JavaScript-first mixed-language example](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40086413598). All nine Node/Bun/Deno combinations on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows passed; all six downstream Rust jobs passed. Both CodeQL language analyses report zero findings, and the three review alerts are fixed. There are 46 successful checks, 10 expected conditional skips, and no failed or pending checks.

Local validation includes full Node, Bun and Deno suites, plus the added preview-token and caller-trigger regressions under all three runtimes. The preview-token and caller-trigger regressions fail before their fixes. Deno's full local suite had three existing runtime capability skips (bin-symlink imports and two CDN command-stream cases). All-warning ESLint, Prettier, jscpd, actionlint, regular/pedantic zizmor, workflow/status-gate policy, both npm audits, Vite build, global-agent proxy bootstrap and Electron directory packaging passed. Runtime suites and builds ran sequentially within the container memory limit; no user caches were deleted. The branch includes the latest main, the full diff has been reviewed, and all 23 required subissues are implemented and verified.

items.title: fix: Repair release guards, credential verification, and CI policies
items.body:
Version and changeset guards could report success after a failed Git comparison, npm preflight could report publishing access without contacting npm, and an interrupted publication could leave its GitHub release missing permanently. This change verifies those states explicitly and completes all seven repairs requested by #212.

## Changes

- **#205:** Compare parsed manifest versions at the merge base and PR head using argument-array Git calls. Formatting passes; unavailable refs, invalid metadata, and manual version changes fail. Release exemptions require a same-repository PR from the configured release actor, rather than a branch prefix alone.
- **#206:** Count added PR fragments only and fail when comparison is unavailable. Directory scanning requires an explicit local opt-in and is forbidden in CI. Document Markdown/excluded-path exemptions; validate optional fragments too. Cover divergent history and multi-language package roots.
- **#207:** Request GitHub's JWT with the npm audience, then POST the package-scoped npm token exchange. Denials, unknown responses, and malformed bodies block release even if Docker succeeds. Returned tokens are discarded without logging. Preserve the documented first-publication `NPM_TOKEN` fallback.
- **#208:** Detect generated npm badges from Markdown image URLs with an exact HTTPS host and npm badge path. Preserve Git commit messages through argument-array execution, verified with an actual temporary repository.
- **#209:** Print survivor records with actual newlines and replace the SIGTERM fixture's EOF busy loop with a blocking wait. Verify separate real child-process records and successful kill escalation.
- **#210:** Use supported zizmor-action v0.6.4 and zizmor 1.30.1 in both passes and the reproduction comment. Pin secretlint and its preset to 13.0.7. Add a policy guard rejecting floating scanner packages and runner labels.
- **#211:** Repair npm-published versions missing a GitHub release with `should_release=true`, `skip_bump=true`, and the existing tag naming helper. Only a release-API 404 means missing; lookup errors remain unknown. Exclude experiments/examples from CodeQL and pin every macOS/Windows runner to `macos-15`/`windows-2025`.

The initial Security run also failed the example lockfile audit on critical Capacitor and high-severity source-map-js advisories. A compatible lockfile refresh clears the configured audit threshold; the example build passes. One patch changeset prepares the automatic release. The prepared placeholder file is removed.

## Requirement audit, research, and reproduction

The [complete requirement inventory and solution analysis](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-212-1433de83b19f/docs/case-studies/issue-212/README.md) maps every requirement to alternatives, the selected plan, and verification. It includes primary documentation, existing components considered (Changesets, Secretlint, zizmor, Octokit, remark, and built-in process/HTTP APIs), repository-wide coverage, and the initial CI errors with log line numbers.

All eight issue descriptions and their comments, recent related merged PRs, and all three PR comment types were inspected. Every listed issue was reproducible; none was already resolved.

Run `node experiments/issue-212-regressions.mjs` to replay the regressions against the isolated pre-fix main snapshot. It records 56 failed assertions across 113 tests, including the original behavioral defects. [Compressed before/after logs](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/tree/issue-212-1433de83b19f/docs/case-studies/issue-212/validation) are committed for review. HTTP tests use local servers or curl stubs and never publish packages.

## Validation

- Node: **559 passed**; Bun: **559 passed**; Deno: **414 applicable tests passed**.
- `npm run check`: lint, formatting, and duplication checks passed.
- Syntax, line limits, required docs, workflow policy, and every status-gate coverage check passed.
- actionlint 1.7.12 and both zizmor 1.30.1 passes passed.
- Pinned secretlint full-tree scan passed. `node experiments/issue-212-secretlint.mjs` verifies clean exit 0 and synthetic GitHub/Slack token exit 1.
- Root and example high-severity audits passed; example clean installation and production build passed.

Remote CI passed at final commit `aad407d38cf290bbb3be5ae033f4ef247dd4e98e`. All five runs were created at `2026-10-07T01:31:52Z`, after that commit: [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37557561665), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37557561686), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37557561716), [Example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37557561857), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37557561656). All nine Node/Bun/Deno × Ubuntu/macOS/Windows test jobs passed, as did desktop packaging on all three operating systems.

The first submitted CI run caught a Windows-only assumption in the new commit-message test: its source matcher required LF while Git checked out CRLF. The added explicit LF/CRLF cases reproduced the failure locally before correcting the matcher; both now verify the exact commit message under Node and Bun. The failed run and before/after logs are preserved in the validation evidence.

The documentation states the chosen documentation-only and release-actor policies. Historical release backfill was suggested as an additional option in #211; the implemented gate repairs the current version on the next qualifying main push. Existing npm recovery, trusted release automation, token bootstrap, and publication-verification protections are retained. The example audit still reports eight pre-existing moderate findings below the configured threshold; its forced fix requires a breaking downgrade.

Fixes #205

Fixes #210
Fixes #211

items.title: `persist-credentials: false` is set on 2 of 27 checkouts (js) / 2 of 11 (php) / 1 of 13 (csharp); zizmor reports the rest but `--min-confidence medium` hides every one of them
items.body:
## Evidence

`actions/checkout` writes the job token into `.git/config` as an
`http.extraheader` and leaves it there for the remainder of the job unless
`persist-credentials: false` is passed. That is zizmor's `artipacked` audit.

Measured at the commits in `../references/templates/*.HEAD`, with zizmor
1.29.0, offline, using each template's own `.github/zizmor.yml`:

```console
# what the template's own gate reports
$ zizmor --offline --config .github/zizmor.yml \
    --persona regular --min-confidence medium .github/workflows

# what is actually there
$ zizmor --offline --config .github/zizmor.yml \
    --persona auditor .github/workflows
```

| template | checkouts | `persist-credentials: false` | artipacked (auditor) | artipacked (own gate) | confidences |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rust | 26 | 26 | 2 | 0 | all Low |
| js | 27 | 2 | **25** | **0** | all Low |
| python | 18 | 18 | 1 | 0 | all Low |
| php | 11 | 2 | **9** | **0** | all Low |
| csharp | 13 | 1 | **12** | **0** | all Low |

rust's 2 and python's 1 are not unswept checkouts. They are the release jobs
that push, and each one says so:

```yaml
      # The only checkout in this repository that keeps credentials in
      # .git/config: scripts/version_and_commit.py runs `git push origin main`
      # to publish the version bump, which needs the token wired into the
      # remote. Every other checkout sets persist-credentials: false.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: true
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```
(`python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/.github/workflows/release.yml:633`)

js, php and csharp never set the input at all. The full per-finding list is in
`../analysis/template-artipacked-sweep.md`; the shape is the same everywhere:

```
js   release.yml   test                  L291   uses: actions/checkout@v6
js   release.yml   lint                  L212   uses: actions/checkout@v6
js   security.yml  npm-audit             L85    uses: actions/checkout@v6
php  release.yml   test                  L136   uses: actions/checkout@v4
php  docs.yml      build                 L41    uses: actions/checkout@v4
csharp release.yml build                 L293   uses: actions/checkout@v6
csharp security.yml codeql               L29    uses: actions/checkout@v6
```

## Why the existing gate does not catch it

Each template's zizmor job runs with `min-confidence: medium`:

```yaml
      - uses: zizmorcore/zizmor-action@v0.6.2
        with:
          advanced-security: false
          annotations: true
          config: .github/zizmor.yml
          min-confidence: medium
```
(`js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/.github/workflows/workflows.yml:64`)

Every `artipacked` finding on a checkout that simply omits the input is emitted
at **Low** confidence -- zizmor cannot prove from the workflow text that the
credential is unused, so it does not claim to. The floor is above the finding.
This is a false negative in the security gate, not an absence of the defect:
the same measurement with `--persona auditor` and no floor returns 25 / 9 / 12.

`csharp` compounds it: that template has no zizmor job and no
`.github/zizmor.yml` at all (already reported as
`csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#53`), so its 12 findings have
no pass that could report them even in principle.

## Reproducible example

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template
$ cd js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template
$ pipx run zizmor==1.29.0 --offline --config .github/zizmor.yml \
    --persona regular --min-confidence medium --format json .github/workflows \
  | jq '[.[] | select(.ident == "artipacked")] | length'
0

$ pipx run zizmor==1.29.0 --offline --config .github/zizmor.yml \
    --persona auditor --format json .github/workflows \
  | jq '[.[] | select(.ident == "artipacked")] | length'
25

$ pipx run zizmor==1.29.0 --offline --config .github/zizmor.yml \
    --persona auditor --format json .github/workflows \
  | jq -r '[.[] | select(.ident == "artipacked")
            | .determinations.confidence] | unique | @csv'
"Low"
```

The last command is the whole report in one line: the findings exist, and they
are all below the floor the gate sets.

## Workaround

For a repository generated from one of these templates, add the input to every
checkout that does not push, and pin the exceptions explicitly:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
```

Until that is done, lower the gate's floor in `.github/workflows/workflows.yml`
to see the findings:

```yaml
        with:
          min-confidence: low
```

That reports them, but it also unfloors every other Low-confidence audit, which
is why it is a workaround and not the fix.

## Suggested fix in code

Three parts, in this order.

**1. Sweep the checkouts that do not push.** The jobs that must keep the
credential are the ones that write to the remote, and they are enumerable:

| template | jobs that push | mechanism | jobs to sweep |
|---|---|---|---|
| js | `release`, `instant-release` | `scripts/version-and-commit.mjs` -> `scripts/push-main-with-rebase-retry.mjs` (`release.yml:515`, `:606`) | 22 of 25 |
| js | `changeset-pr` | `peter-evans/create-pull-request` (`release.yml:828`) | |
| php | `auto-release`, `manual-release` | `scripts/version-and-commit.php` -> `VersionReleaser` -> `Git::push` (`release.yml:263`, `:319`) | 7 of 9 |
| csharp | `release`, `instant-release` | `scripts/version-and-commit.mjs:423` `git push` / `:424` `git push --tags` (`release.yml:418`, `:614`) | 9 of 12 |
| csharp | `changeset-pr` | `peter-evans/create-pull-request` (`release.yml:776`) | |

Everything else -- `lint`, `test`, `build`, `detect-changes`, `docker-*`,
`codeql`, `dependency-review`, `npm-audit`, `link-checker`, `docs`,
`pipeline-status` -- fetches and never writes, so it can drop the credential.
Public-repository fetches still work with no credential at all, which is worth
verifying rather than assuming:

```console
$ git init -q && git remote add origin https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
$ GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/true git fetch --depth=1 origin main
From https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>
 * branch            main       -> FETCH_HEAD
```

Do this direction carefully: sweeping a job that *does* push removes the only
credential its release has, and the failure surfaces only on `main`, after the
package is already published. Downstream this was gotten wrong once and is
written up in
[`analysis/artipacked-sweep.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/dev/log/issues/1079/pulls/1080/analysis/artipacked-sweep.md#the-two-the-first-pass-of-this-sweep-broke).

**2. Make each exception carry its reason.** The python template's comment
above is the model: name the push the credential exists for.

**3. Make the invariant a test, not a habit.** A swept tree regresses the first
time someone adds a job. Two assertions over the workflow text are enough, and
they are the reason the sweep stays swept:

* every checkout sets `persist-credentials: false` unless its job writes to the
  remote (`git push`, the version-and-commit script, `create-pull-request`),
  and the exception count is pinned to an exact number;
* no job that writes to the remote sets `persist-credentials: false`.

Downstream these are
`tests/unit/issue_1079.rs::every_checkout_drops_its_credential_unless_it_pushes`
and `::every_job_that_pushes_still_has_a_credential_to_push_with`. In the js and
csharp templates the natural home is `tests/ci-timeouts.test.js`'s neighbours;
in php, `tests/` beside the other workflow assertions.

Raising `min-confidence` to `low` is deliberately *not* the recommendation on
its own: it reports 25 findings and an unmeasured number of unrelated
Low-confidence ones in the same run, which is how a gate gets an allowlist
instead of a fix.

items.title: artipacked is invisible to the zizmor job: min-confidence medium hides all 25 checkouts that persist credentials
items.body:
`actions/checkout` leaves the job token in `.git/config` unless it is told not
to. In this template 25 of the 27 checkouts leave it there, and the workflow
that is supposed to catch exactly that cannot report it.

## The blind spot

`.github/workflows/workflows.yml` runs:

```yaml
      - uses: zizmorcore/zizmor-action@v0.6.2
        with:
          advanced-security: false
          annotations: true
          config: .github/zizmor.yml
          min-confidence: medium
```

zizmor's `artipacked` audit reports at **Low** confidence, so
`min-confidence: medium` filters every instance out. Run against this
repository's own workflows with its own config:

```console
$ zizmor --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence medium .github/workflows
58 findings (33 ignored, 22 suppressed, 3 safe fixes): 0 informational, 3 low, 0 medium, 0 high

$ zizmor --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence low .github/workflows
58 findings (1 ignored, 22 suppressed, 3 safe fixes, 32 unsafe fixes): 7 informational, 28 low, 0 medium, 0 high

$ zizmor --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence low .github/workflows | grep -c 'help\[artipacked\]'
25
```

(zizmor 1.30.0. The three findings still visible at `medium` are the
`self-repository` ones from #155.)

Sample:

```
help[artipacked]: credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts
  --> .github/workflows/links.yml:43:9
   |
43 |       - uses: actions/checkout@v6
   |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ does not set persist-credentials: false
   |
   = note: audit confidence → Low
   = note: this finding has an auto-fix
```

## Where

Every checkout except the two in `workflows.yml`:

| Workflow          | Jobs                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `release.yml`     | `detect-changes`, `test-compilation`, `check-file-line-limits`, `version-check`, `changeset-check`, `lint`, `test`, `docker-build`, `validate-docs`, `docker-publish-config`, `docker-publish-build`, `docker-publish`, `pipeline-status` (read-only) and `release`, `instant-release`, `changeset-pr` (`contents: write`) |
| `security.yml`    | `codeql`, `dependency-review`, `npm-audit`                                                                                                                                             |
| `example-app.yml` | `web-build`, `desktop-package`, `android-build`, `ios-build`, `preview-regen`                                                                                                          |
| `links.yml`       | `link-checker`                                                                                                                                                                         |

The Rust template is the counter-example: there, every checkout sets
`persist-credentials: false` except the two jobs that actually push
(`auto-release`, `manual-release` in `release.yml`), which is what a deliberate
decision looks like.

## Why it matters

The read-only jobs are the ones worth fixing first, and `lint` and `test` most
of all: both check out a pull-request branch, run `npm install` on it, and then
run that branch's code. A `postinstall` script or a compromised transitive
dependency can read `.git/config` and use the token for as long as the job runs;
anything that uploads the workspace (or a `.git`-containing subdirectory) as an
artifact publishes it outright. That is the whole point of the `artipacked`
audit, and this repository has switched it off by accident.

## Reproduction

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template
$ cd js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template
$ pipx run zizmor==1.30.0 --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence medium .github/workflows   # 0 artipacked
$ pipx run zizmor==1.30.0 --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence low    .github/workflows   # 25 artipacked
```

Or inside a job, without zizmor:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - run: git config --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader   # prints AUTHORIZATION: basic ***
```

## Workaround

Add `persist-credentials: false` to the checkouts by hand; the audit that would
have found the next one stays off.

## Suggested fix

1. Set `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout in a job that does not
   push:

   ```diff
        - uses: actions/checkout@v6
   +      with:
   +        persist-credentials: false
   ```

   `zizmor --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence low --fix=all
   .github/workflows` applies this, but its fixes are `unsafe` here precisely
   because of the three writer jobs — review those three (`release`,
   `instant-release`, `changeset-pr`) and keep their credentials.

2. Then lower the workflow's threshold so a new checkout cannot re-introduce it:

   ```diff
          config: .github/zizmor.yml
   -      min-confidence: medium
   +      min-confidence: low
   ```

   After step 1 that leaves ~10 findings, all in the informational/low bucket
   and each either fixable or suppressible with a `# zizmor: ignore[...]`
   comment that records the reason — which is strictly better than a threshold
   that hides an entire audit.

Found while auditing CI/CD against this template for
link-foundation/command-stream#199.
